# CHD-3.3 Revision Plan
> **Status:** implementation plan derived from the CHD-3.2 review package. This is a plan for revising the authored handbook and its companion contracts; it is not an implementation claim, a render result, or owner acceptance. > > **Source authority:** `review/chd32-package/00-START-HERE.txt`, `01-REVISION-HANDOFF.txt`, `02-DETAILED-FEEDBACK.txt`, canonical `03-REVIEW-LOG.json`, and the unchanged baseline files `04-BASELINE-AUTHORING-BRIEF.txt` and `05-BASELINE-TEN-WORKFLOWS.txt`. The review log is authoritative for all 27 R32 findings, all 30 R31 dispositions, and D-039.

## 1. Goal and non-negotiable invariants
CHD-3.3 must be a self-contained, internally consistent build specification for general-purpose director-led coordination of configured Hermes agents. Hermes remains responsible for cognition, learning, native sessions and provider fallback. CHD owns durable shared work, controller ticket state, admission, delegation, threaded routing, reports, evidence, archives and recovery contracts.
The revision is complete only when a competent implementer can resolve every normative reference from the delivered package, implement each supported operation without inventing fields or behavior, and run the supplied fixture suite. Specification status, source cross-check, implementation, measured execution and owner acceptance remain separate states.
**Global invariants to apply to every affected file and generated view:**
1. `send_id`, `attempt_id`, `run_id`, request identity and native target identity are distinct; exact replay never changes its target or idempotency key. 2. Native session creation/fork provisioning and `NEW`/`REUSE` delivery are distinct operations. A returned Hermes child id is persisted before its first turn. 3. A logical send, an attempt, a wait/gate, a run and a report have separate records and transitions. Waiting closes an attempt but leaves the logical send open; a successor is explicit. 4. Only proven stop releases capacity. Lease expiry, timeout, process exit, a report, cancellation intent or a lost response is not stop proof. 5. All multi-record effects use an implementable journal/commit-marker or equivalent protocol on the supported substrate. Unacknowledged execution is unknown until reconciliation. 6. Use, `grant_use`, `meta_grant` and `create` are independent authority classes. A grantor may grant without use; no class implies another. 7. D-038 remains the fork rule: `preserve_parent_snapshot` is the default, `current_policy` is the explicit alternate, resync is explicit and authorized, and live sessions never auto-resync. 8. **D-039 applies to every restore/import/replacement restore:** resolve CURRENT permissions on every restore. The archived policy is audit/history only and never becomes the replacement's effective authority automatically. Restore always creates a new profile/session/bond and records old-to-new identity and both policy revisions. 9. Diagrams, registers, tables, schemas, examples, fixtures and generated indexes derive from the same canonical definitions. 10. A named file, hash, figure, test ID or green build is not evidence that its content was delivered or executed.

## 2. Delivery order and dependency gates
Implement in this order; a later ticket must not establish a competing contract for a field or state owned by an earlier ticket.
1. **Identity and canonical state:** T02, T05, T07, T09, T10, T11. Freeze record identities, state transitions, attempt/run/wait semantics, policy lifetimes and commit boundaries. 2. **Package and contract inventory:** T01, T03, T04, T06, T08, T12, T13, T16. Make every cited file real, versioned and mechanically linked. 3. **Recovery and federation:** T12, T13, T14, T15. Apply D-039 and the proven-stop/current-policy rules to all recovery and bridge paths. 4. **Derived views and acceptance:** T02, T14, T15, T16. Regenerate diagrams/registers from canonical definitions; replace stale workflow expectations; classify evidence honestly.
A ticket may touch multiple files, but only the owning section defines the normative rule. Explanatory sections and figures link to that rule rather than restating variants.

## 4. D-039 propagation checklist (must be checked as a set)
D-039 is a cross-cutting owner decision, not only R32-027.
